intervals.label: commissioning after completion of construction
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Booster'
intervals.note: Start is the completion of construction (21 December 1970); the end is the day the Booster reached its design energy of 8 GeV (21 May 1971), after which it is recorded as operating. No source fetched gives a groundbreaking date for the ring, so no construction interval is written.
intervals.quote: The lab completed construction of the Booster on December 21, 1970.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Booster'
intervals.note: Start is the day the Booster achieved its design energy of 8 GeV (21 May 1971). NuMI beam data taking from 20 May 2005 (NuMI beam paper) documents it as operating in the neutrino era. REPLACED 2026-10-25: the earlier start ('in operation by 2005; earliest 1968') was an evidence date, not a start.
intervals.quote: The Booster achieved its design energy of 8 GeV on May 21, 1971.

beam_energy.locator: §4.2 NuMI Mode of Operation; arXiv PDF p. 50
beam_energy.quote: The Booster then accelerates those protons to 8 GeV.

circumference.quote: The FNAL Booster is a 474-meter-circumference synchrotron operating at 15Hz.

summary.plain: A rapid-cycling ring 474 metres around that takes protons to 8 billion electronvolts. It feeds the Booster neutrino beam and the rest of the Fermilab chain.
summary.technical: 474 m circumference rapid-cycling synchrotron running at 15 Hz, accelerating protons from 400 MeV to 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c) for the BNB and for injection into the Recycler and Main Injector.
